config.title: Build password reset flow

intro.title: Build password reset flow
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a password reset flow for a Node.js application, allowing users to securely reset their passwords via email. You will learn how to generate unique reset tokens, send emails with reset links, and handle token validation and password updates. The core programming concepts include using environment variables for security, managing asynchronous operations with async/await, and implementing basic routing and error handling. You will work with technologies like Node.js, Express for routing, Nodemailer for sending emails, and a simple in-memory store for demonstration purposes. By the end, you will have a functional reset flow that demonstrates real-world backend security practices.
intro.usecase: Password reset flows are essential security features in nearly every web application that requires user authentication. You'll implement this pattern in user account settings, login screens, and security dashboards where users need to recover access to their accounts. As a Node.js developer, you'll build these flows for e-commerce platforms, banking applications, SaaS products, and social media sites to handle forgotten credentials securely. This involves creating time-limited reset tokens, validating user identity, and ensuring password updates follow security best practices while providing a smooth user experience.

objectives: Implement a password reset request endpoint that validates user email
Configure token generation and expiration for password reset links
Construct a password reset email template with secure token integration
Initialize a password update endpoint that validates reset tokens
Apply password hashing and validation when updating user credentials
Manipulate user database records to update password fields securely
Control error handling for invalid tokens and expired reset requests

steps.title: Import required Node.js modules
steps.instruction: At the top of your file, import the crypto, nodemailer, and express modules using require() statements.
steps.hint: Use require('module-name') to import each module. Place all three import statements at the beginning of the file.
steps.seedCode:
// Import required modules here

// Your password reset flow code will go below
steps.expectedOutcome: Your file will have three require() statements at the top, making the crypto, nodemailer, and express modules available for use.
successCriteria: crypto, nodemailer, and express modules are imported using require() statements at the top of the file.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but you need to import all three modules: crypto, nodemailer, and express. Make sure you're using require() statements for each one.
steps.feedbackWrong: import three specific modules: crypto (for generating tokens), nodemailer (for sending emails), and express (for creating the web server). Use require() statements for each at the top of your file.

steps.title: Initialize Express application
steps.instruction: Create an Express application instance and store it in a constant variable named 'app'.
steps.hint: Use the imported Express module to create an Express application instance.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating an Express app instance
const app = express();
steps.expectedOutcome: An Express application instance is created and assigned to a constant variable named 'app'.
successCriteria: The code includes a constant variable 'app' initialized with express()
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you create a constant variable named 'app' and initialize it with express().
steps.feedbackWrong: The Express application instance wasn't created correctly. You need to create a constant variable named 'app' and initialize it with express().

steps.title: Create in-memory user storage
steps.instruction: Create an array named 'users' to store user objects with 'email' and 'password' fields. Initialize it with at least one user for testing.
steps.hint: You can create an array of objects where each object has email and password properties. For example: [{ email: 'test@example.com', password: 'hashedPassword123' }]
steps.expectedOutcome: An array named 'users' is created with at least one user object containing email and password fields.
successCriteria: The 'users' array exists and contains at least one object with 'email' and 'password' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your array is named 'users' and contains objects with both 'email' and 'password' fields.
steps.feedbackWrong: The user storage wasn't created correctly. Please create an array named 'users' with at least one user object containing email and password properties.

steps.title: Create password reset token storage
steps.instruction: Create an object to store password reset tokens. The object should be a constant named 'resetTokens' initialized as an empty array.
steps.hint: Use 'const resetTokens = [];' to create an empty array for storing token objects.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating an array for temporary data
const temporaryData = [];
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a 'resetTokens' array ready to store token objects with email, token, and expiry properties.
successCriteria: A constant named 'resetTokens' is declared and initialized as an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've declared 'resetTokens' as a constant and initialized it as an empty array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The reset token storage wasn't created correctly. You need to declare a constant named 'resetTokens' and set it to an empty array.

steps.title: Define password reset request handler
steps.instruction: Create a POST route handler for '/api/reset-password' that validates the email exists in your users array and generates a reset token.
steps.hint: Use app.post() to define the route. Check if the email exists in the users array, then generate a token and store it in resetTokens.
steps.expectedOutcome: A POST route handler for '/api/reset-password' that validates email and generates a reset token.
successCriteria: Route handler is defined with app.post('/api/reset-password', ...), checks if email exists in users array, generates a token, and stores it in resetTokens.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your handler validates the email exists and generates/stores a token.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handler is missing or incomplete. Check that you've defined a POST route for '/api/reset-password' with proper validation and token generation.

steps.title: Generate secure reset token
steps.instruction: Inside your password reset request handler, generate a secure token using crypto.randomBytes() and set an expiration time 1 hour from now.
steps.hint: Use crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex') to create a 64-character hex token. Create an expiration date with Date.now() + 3600000.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your handler should now generate a cryptographically secure token and calculate its expiration time.
successCriteria: The handler includes token generation using crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex') and sets expiresAt to Date.now() + 3600000.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex') for the token and Date.now() + 3600000 for the expiration.
steps.feedbackWrong: The token generation or expiration logic is missing or incorrect. Review the crypto module documentation for generating secure random bytes.

steps.title: Create email sending function
steps.instruction: Create a function named sendResetEmail that takes email and token parameters and logs a message about sending the email.
steps.hint: Define a function that accepts email and token parameters and uses console.log to output a message containing those values.
steps.expectedOutcome: A sendResetEmail function is defined that accepts email and token parameters and logs a message.
successCriteria: The sendResetEmail function is defined with email and token parameters and includes a console.log statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function is named sendResetEmail, accepts both email and token parameters, and includes a console.log statement.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Create a function named sendResetEmail that takes email and token parameters and logs a message about sending the email.

steps.title: Define password update handler
steps.instruction: Create a POST route handler for '/api/update-password' that validates the reset token and updates the user's password.
steps.hint: Add a new app.post() route after your existing '/api/reset-password' route. The handler should check if the token exists and hasn't expired, then find the user and update their password.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new POST route '/api/update-password' is added with a handler function that validates tokens and updates passwords.
successCriteria: The code includes a POST route handler for '/api/update-password' that validates reset tokens and updates user passwords.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the route, but make sure it's a POST route for '/api/update-password' and includes token validation logic.
steps.feedbackWrong: The password update handler isn't properly defined. Create a POST route for '/api/update-password' that validates tokens and updates passwords.

steps.title: Implement token validation logic
steps.instruction: Inside the password update handler, add validation logic to check if the provided token exists in resetTokens storage and hasn't expired.
steps.hint: Look up the token in resetTokens array and compare its expiration timestamp with the current time.
steps.expectedOutcome: The password update handler will include token existence and expiration checks before allowing password changes.
successCriteria: The handler validates token existence in resetTokens and checks expiration timestamp.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some validation, but make sure to check both token existence and expiration. Look for the token in resetTokens and compare expires with Date.now().
steps.feedbackWrong: The token validation logic is missing or incorrect. The handler should verify the token exists in resetTokens and hasn't expired before allowing password updates.

steps.title: Add password hashing function
steps.instruction: Create a function named hashPassword that takes a password string as a parameter and returns a hashed version using crypto.createHash('sha256').
steps.hint: Use crypto.createHash('sha256') to create a hash, then update it with the password and output it as hex.
steps.expectedOutcome: A hashPassword function that securely hashes passwords using SHA-256.
successCriteria: The hashPassword function is defined, takes a password parameter, uses crypto.createHash('sha256'), and returns the hashed password as a hex string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function takes a password parameter, uses crypto.createHash('sha256'), and returns the hashed value as hex.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't quite right. Create a function named hashPassword that hashes passwords using crypto.createHash('sha256').

steps.title: Set up server routes
steps.instruction: Register the reset password and update password route handlers with the Express app by calling app.use() to enable JSON body parsing and ensure the routes are properly mounted.
steps.hint: Use app.use(express.json()) to parse JSON request bodies, then ensure your existing app.post() routes are correctly placed after this middleware.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Express app will be configured to parse JSON request bodies and handle the two password reset routes.
successCriteria: app.use(express.json()) is added before the route handlers, and both app.post() routes remain in the code.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added the JSON body parsing middleware and kept both route handlers.
steps.feedbackWrong: The routes aren't properly set up. Check that you've added app.use(express.json()) and that both app.post() routes are present.

steps.title: Start the Express server
steps.instruction: Start the Express server by calling the listen method on port 3000 and log a startup message.
steps.hint: Use app.listen() with the port number and a callback function that logs a message.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will start and be accessible via HTTP, enabling the password reset flow endpoints.
successCriteria: The Express server is started on port 3000 with a console log message indicating it's running.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the server, but make sure to include a console log message in the callback.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server isn't started yet. Use app.listen() with port 3000 and a callback that logs a message.
